qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 generally available. The release describes stronger coding-agent performance, Programmatic Tool Calling for in-memory programs that coordinate tools and filter intermediate data, multi-agent support in beta, explicit cache breakpoints, and published model-size pricing.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest only the local practice implications for tool-call governance, harness design, and cost telemetry; route model-family background upstream.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local tool-governance and harness guidance should distinguish model-driven tool calls from program-controlled intermediate processing, and cost telemetry guidance may need to capture model-size, cache, and multi-agent concurrency tradeoffs.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Work and said the Codex app is merging into the ChatGPT desktop app with inline editing in diffs, pull-request review in the side panel, faster computer use powered by GPT-5.6, and support for multiple repositories in one project.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep product facts upstream; locally review whether multi-repo workspaces alter file-boundary and handoff guidance.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Request packages, handoffs, and persistent workspace practices may need to account for multi-repository task scope, side-panel PR review, and inline diff editing as first-class review surfaces.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Codex changelog records a July 9 desktop integration with direct Markdown/code editing, inline annotations, PR sidebar review, multi-repository projects, faster computer use, and clearer task progress. July 9 CLI 0.144.0 added writes app-approval mode, interactive MCP authentication, hosted app-server authentication, and an Ultra concurrency warning. July 13 iOS notes added inline visualizations in Codex tasks plus task-link and progress improvements. July 14 CLI 0.144.4 was a no-user-facing-change patch.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Do not ingest version-only patch entries except as exclusions; review the July 9/13 items for local workflow implications.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Approval modes, MCP authentication, concurrency warnings, inline review, and task-progress surfaces are local operating concerns for request boundaries, tool governance, coordination limits, and progress telemetry.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GSA updated its 2026 Model Context Protocol Server and AI Agent Hackathon page. The page frames MCP as a standard for connecting autonomous agents to real-world data and services, with a federal hackathon focused on open data assets, service-delivery use cases, compatible clients, local testing, JSON-RPC/HTTP/SSE transport, and read/write API integration.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route ecosystem/entity background upstream; keep only the local practice implication around governed service-bound tool design.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local MCP practice lens can treat public-sector MCP work as an example of domain-expert-owned tool servers, governed read/write APIs, and workflow/service-delivery grounding before model selection.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Augment Code described AI incident-management workflows in which agents centralize metrics, traces, logs, deployment history, and ownership metadata, using parallel investigation against observability APIs and producing a linked evidence bundle for responders.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Confirm page-visible dates during ingest; if accepted, synthesize as an evidence-bundle practice rather than product coverage.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The source reinforces that evidence bundles should be structured around linked artifacts and ownership metadata, not just a generated narrative, when agents investigate code or operational incidents.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Open Agent Skills published a deep review of Repo Task Proof Loop, a compact Apache-2.0 project that turns an agent completion claim into repository evidence through specifications, evidence, and independent verification; it recorded 720 stars and 45 forks as of July 13, 2026.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: If ingested, keep the local lens on proof-loop practices and route project background upstream if the upstream AI wiki owns tool entities.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Delegated coding and verification-loop guidance can use this as a public example of converting done claims into auditable repo state and independent review artifacts.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Developers Digest argued that dockerless verification is becoming a coding-agent bottleneck and cited checks against a Dockerless arXiv paper, Hugging Face paper page, the Hugging Face July 2026 monthly papers page, SWE-bench, and Google Trends query clusters on July 12, 2026.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: During ingest, prefer primary paper or project sources before relying on this commentary for durable guidance.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The update is relevant to local guidance about when to use compose/build verification versus lighter execution paths, and about making verification constraints explicit in agent harnesses.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI release notes say ChatGPT search across chats, projects, images, and documents is available globally, with filters and direct opening of matched artifacts.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: This selected batch did not include the context-architecture leaves, so use it only as adjacent evidence if those leaves are later selected.
